'''''Ranunculus lanuginosus''''', commonly known as the '''wooly buttercup'''<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|date=2012-07-03|title=Ranunculus lanuginosus|url=https://davisla.wordpress.com/2012/07/03/pllant-of-the-week-ranunculus-lanuginosus/|access-date=2021-08-28|website=landscape architect's pages|language=en}}</ref> and '''downy buttercup''',<ref>{{Cite web|title=Downy Buttercup - Encyclopedia of Life|url=https://eol.org/pages/5524338|access-date=2021-08-28|website=eol.org}}</ref> is a [[Herbaceous plant|herbaceous]] [[Perennial plant|perennial]] plant species in the family [[Ranunculaceae]],<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Kosmata zlatica - Urbanatura|url=https://www.urbanatura.si/vsebina/682/Kosmata-zlatica|access-date=2021-08-28|website=www.urbanatura.si|language=sl}}</ref> that grows in some parts of [[Europe]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Species information: R. lanuginosus L.|url=https://www.infoflora.ch/en/flora/ranunculus-lanuginosus.html|access-date=2021-08-28|website=www.infoflora.ch}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Ranunculus lanuginosus L. {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science|url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:713050-1|access-date=2021-08-28|website=Plants of the World Online|language=en}}</ref>

== Etymology ==
The plant's [[genus]] name comes from a Latin term ''rana'', which means "frog", referring to the buttercup's typical moist and shaded habitats. On the other hand, species' name ''lanuginosus'' derives from a Latin word ''lanugo'', which is translated as "downy" and refers to the plant's stem, covered with a layer of fine hair.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":4">{{Cite web|title=Scheda IPFI, Acta Plantarum Ranunculus_lanuginosus|url=https://www.actaplantarum.org/flora/flora_info.php?id=6348|access-date=2021-08-28|website=www.actaplantarum.org}}</ref>

== Taxonomy ==
This species was first described by Swedish naturalist [[Carl Linnaeus]] in his famous work [[Species Plantarum|''Species plantarum'']] in 1753.<ref name=":gbif">{{Cite web|title=Ranunculus lanuginosus L.|url=https://www.gbif.org/species/7826351|access-date=2021-08-28|website=www.gbif.org|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Ranunculus lanuginosus L. — The Plant List|url=http://www.theplantlist.org/tpl1.1/record/kew-2523789|access-date=2021-08-28|website=www.theplantlist.org}}</ref>

There are a few recognized [[Variety (botany)|varieties]] of this species:<ref name=":gbif" />

* ''Ranunculus lanuginosus'' var. ''geraniifolius'' [[DC.]], 1817
* ''Ranunculus lanuginosus'' var. ''lanuginosus''
* ''Ranunculus lanuginosus'' var. ''parvulus'' DC., 1824
* ''Ranunculus lanuginosus'' var. ''umbrosus'' (Ten. & [[Guss.]]) P.Fourn., 1936

== Description ==
''Ranunculus lanuginosus'' is herbaceous and perennial [[buttercup]] that can reach from 30 to 80 centimetres of height. It is usually an upright-growing and spread out plant that has stem with dense layer of [[trichome]]s. This species' stem is round and thick, as well as hollow. Its basal leaves have long leafstalk and are [[palmately]] [[lobed]]; with five segments being [[Ovate (botany)|ovate]] and hirsute, while having double serrated margin. Upper stem leaves are sessile and palmately lobed, with wide segments.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":0" /> In most cases, leaves measure 12 centimetres in length and 8 centimetres in width.<ref name=":3" />

''Ranunculus lanuginosus'' is an [[entomophilous]] species<ref name=":3" /> that flowers between May and August.<ref name=":1" /> This buttercup has yellow to orange flowers with darker middle area and five floral leaves in both corolla and calyx.<ref name=":0" /> Each flower measures from 2 to 2.5 centimetres.<ref name=":1" /> Calyx has hairy [[sepal]]s. The plant's fruit is so-called [[achene]]; it is hairless and laterally squeezed, while it ends with long and curved rostrum.<ref name=":0" />

As many other buttercups, wooly buttercup is toxic.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web|title=Search for species - Wolliger Hahnenfuß (Ranunculus lanuginosus L.)|url=https://www.i-flora.com/en/fact-sheets/search-for-species/art/show/ranunculus-lanuginosus.html|access-date=2021-08-28|website=www.i-flora.com}}</ref>

== Distribution ==
''Ranunculus lanuginosus'' is a European plant species that occurs in middle and southern Europe, as well as in [[Caucasus]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ranunculus lanuginosus (kosmata zlatica)|url=http://www.botanicni-vrt.si/component/rastline/ranunculus-lanuginosus|access-date=2021-08-28|website=www.botanicni-vrt.si}}</ref> ''R. lanuginosus'' is a [[native species]] of Albania, Austria, Baltic States, Bulgaria, Corsica, Czechoslovakia, Denmark, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Italy, Poland, Romania, Sardinia, Sicilia, Switzerland, Turkey (in Europe), Ukraine and former Yugoslavian countries.<ref name=":2" />

This relatively common buttercup species can be found growing in various shaded forests with dense [[undergrowth]], as well as in other similar shaded and humid places.<ref name=":0" /> The [[Raunkiær system]] classifies it as a [[hemicryptophyte]] species.<ref name=":1" /> ''Ranunculus lanuginosus'' is primarily a lowland species that only rarely grows in [[subalpine]] zone with maximal elevations of around 1,400.<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":4" />
